full_judgment:
13. On 25.03.2001 Jamal Uddin Ahmed filed an application before the High Court Division under section 46 of the Trade Marks Act, 1940 for rectification of the Register of Trade Marks by removal of the registered Trade Mark No.38818 in Class-6, giving rise to Trade Mark Application No.4 of 2001. In substance, his claim was that Abdul Haque, proprietor of Sathi Metal Industries, in the name of manufacturing C.I. Fittings in Class-6 was actually manufacturing sanitary goods with the trademark "LUCKY". After hearing the parties, the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 13.02.2002 allowed the petition cancelling the trademark "LUCKY" in respect of C.I. Fittings under No.38818 in Class-6. Respondent No.1, Abdul Haque filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1106 of 2002, which was dismissed by this Division on 13.07.2003. In addition Jamal Uddin Ahmed filed Petition Case No.1305 of 2001 dated 29.03.2001 under sections 482/483/486 of the Penal Code, which having been dismissed, Revision Case No.555 of 2001 was filed before the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka. 

 16. The Deputy Registrar of Trade Marks, Dhaka, by his order dated 15.10.2003 rejected Opposition Case No.1881 of 2001 finding that the opposer could not prove his case and thereby accepted application No.66491 in Class-6 for registration. The Deputy Registrar of Trade Marks observed that international classification list contains C.I. pipe fittings and manhole cover within goods of Class-6 and not Class-11. He also observed that the Nice Agreement shows pipes of metal, water pipes of metal, gutter pipes of metal, cast iron unwrought or semi-wrought, cast steel, fittings of metal for building, manhole covers of metal are goods within Class-6. Hence, there was no doubt that application No.66491 was for goods with-in Class-6 and therefore, registration of such goods in Class-6 could not be hindered. By registration of goods in Class-11 the Deputy Registrar of Trade Marks, Dhaka found that both the applicant and the opposer were manufacturing and marketing different goods using their individual Trade Marks and there is no imitation or deception. 

 31. It is patently clear that the appellant previously manufactured his goods (the same goods as he is now manufacturing) under the trademark 'Lucky' of which the title was assigned to him, but that trade-mark registration No.38818 is class 6 under the mark "Lucky" was removed from the Trade Marks Register by order of the High Court Division passed in Trade Mark Application No.04 of 2001. That removal was upheld by this Division on 13.07.2003. The appellant is now manufacturing and marketing the very same goods under the trademark 'Lucky Star'. The High Court Division in the impugned judgment concluded that this was in violation of sections 8 and 10 of the Trade Marks Act, 1940. In this regard reference may be made to the decision in the case of Baby food products Ltd. Aga Nawab Dowry, Dhaka v. Nabisco Biscuit and Bread Factory Ltd. 262, Tejgaon Industrial Area Dhaka and. another 30BLD(AD)25. In the cited case the respondent manufactured and marketed biscuits under the trademark "Nabisco", whereas the appellants manufactured and marketed goods imitating the trademark of the respondent and secretly filed an application for registration of the trademark consisting of a deceptively similar trademark `Nabico'. This Division held as follows: "It appears that whatever product the petitioner is producing and selling in the trade name of NABICO is likely to deceive the people at large who will presume the products to be of NABISCO being misled by the similarity in sounds and as such this is no ground to review our judgment already passed."
